title: רב דניאל בר רב קטינא

paragraphs: Rav Daniel, son of Rav Katina, said in the name of Rav: Bava Kamma 97, beginning of side a; Moed Katan 8, end of side b, and 12, end of side a; Chagigah 8b; chapter Ellu Terefot. He reported Rav Huna: Ketubbot 97a. Rav Chanan, son of Rav Katina, was his brother. There is a version with Rav Shmuel, son of Rav Katina, and Rabbah bar bar Chana held his son’s wedding in Rav Daniel’s house. This is not so, for he held his son’s wedding in Rabbi Shmuel bar Katina’s house (see his entry). One cannot say that a scribe omitted words and it should read “in the house of Rabbi Shmuel, brother of Rabbi Daniel,” for then this is not its place: there, under Shmuel bar Katina’s name, he did not mention that Rabbah bar bar Chana held his son’s wedding in his house. In Rabbi Ammi’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter Kirah. In Rav Huna’s name: there, end of Eruvin chapter 1, and chapter 2. It is already known that Rabbi Zeira was called Rav Katina because he was small of stature. In the Jerusalem Talmud too, Rabbi Zeira is called Rabbi Zeira [זעירא]. Perhaps Rabbi Daniel’s father is someone else, since Rabbi Zeira responds to the words of Rabbi Daniel, son of Rav Katina, without varying their names, as stated in chapter Ellu Terefot (I did not find it). Rabbi Zeira sent a question to Rav Daniel, son of Rav Katina: “Did you hear from your father?” Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Lulav VaAravah. He had a garden; every day he would say, “This bed needs water, and this bed does not need water,” and rain would come and water where water was needed: Taanit 9b. Sefer Gilgulei Neshamot writes, from the secret of the verse in Zechariah, “He will also give a man rain, grass in the field”: the aforementioned Rav Daniel is an implantation of Gideon, who asked that there be dryness on the fleece and afterwards rain on the fleece alone. As was the deed of the first, so was the deed of the last. End of quotation.
